genes/MYCTU/Rv3395c/Rv3395c-ai-review.ya.description: Rv3395c, designated ImuA', is the accessory partner of ImuB in the mycobacterial damage-induced mutagenesis cassette. It is restricted largely to actinomycetes and is not a homolog of proteobacterial ImuA; it instead resembles RecA at the structural level while lacking RecA's C-terminal domain and nucleotide-binding motif. Deletion of Rv3395c abolishes damage-induced mutagenesis and damage tolerance as completely as deletion of imuB or dnaE2, and ImuA' binds ImuB directly through the C-terminal regions of both proteins. No catalytic or nucleic-acid-binding activity has been demonstrated for it.

review.summary: The membrane location is a UniProt subcellular-location mapping that rests on a single predicted transmembrane helix, and it fits poorly with the protein's demonstrated role.
review.reason: The row derives from the UniProt keyword-to-GO mapping of a SUBCELLULAR LOCATION line whose evidence is curator inference (ECO:0000305) over one sequence-analysis TRANSMEM prediction (ECO:0000255) at residues 63-83; there is no experimental localization. ImuA' acts as a direct ImuB partner in chromosomal damage tolerance, so a single-pass membrane anchor is unlikely to be its functional location, although a hydrophobic segment is genuinely present and the claim is not contradicted by any measurement. Left in place as a flagged over-annotation rather than removed.

knowledge_gaps.gap_statement: What ImuA' does biochemically is unknown: it has a RecA-like fold but lacks the RecA nucleotide-binding motif, and neither DNA binding nor any catalytic activity has been tested.

knowledge_gaps.significance: Whether ImuA' delivers the cassette to single-stranded DNA, as its RecA-like fold suggests, determines how the mutasome finds its substrate and whether it can be targeted separately from DnaE2.

genes/MYCTU/Rv3394c/Rv3394c-ai-review.ya.description: Rv3394c is the ImuB protein of the mycobacterial damage-induced mutagenesis cassette. It retains the UmuC/Y-family polymerase fold but has lost the active-site carboxylates required for catalysis, which UniProt records as a caution on propagating the UmuC feature annotation. Instead of synthesizing DNA it acts as the interaction hub of the cassette, binding ImuA', DnaE1, DnaE2 and the beta clamp; a clamp-binding motif mutant loses cassette function as completely as a deletion. Deletion of Rv3394c abolishes damage-induced mutagenesis and damage tolerance, placing it in the same pathway as Rv3395c (ImuA') and dnaE2.

review.summary: A PAINT inference placed at a node of PTHR35369 and seeded by this very gene's experimental annotation; the claim is sound for ImuB but the term is the broad one the seed carried.
review.reason: The IBA inherits whatever term the IBD node carries, and here the IBD at PANTHER:PTN002176549 was seeded by UniProtKB:O50419 itself, i.e. by this gene's own MTBBASE annotation. Appearing in its own WITH/FROM is the expected marker that experimental grounding exists on the target, not circularity, so the row is kept rather than removed. What it should say is the specific process the seed experiment demonstrates: lesion tolerance with induced mutagenesis, not repair. The breadth of the node is adjudicated in the PTHR35369 family review, where the family also contains SulA cell-division inhibitors for which DNA repair does not hold.

source_entities.comment: The target is its own IBD seed. That is the expected marker that experimental grounding exists on the target itself, not circularity: this gene's MTBBASE annotation from PMID:20615954 is one of the descendant evidences the PAINT curator used to place the node, and the IBA then adds the claim that the role is inherited rather than lineage-specific.

The node carries only the broad DNA repair term, so the inherited claim stops short of what the seed experiment shows. The family also contains the SulA cell-division inhibitors, for which DNA repair does not hold; the node's depth is adjudicated in the PTHR35369 family review.

genes/MYCTU/dnaE2/dnaE2-ai-review.yaml.description: DnaE2 (Rv3370c) is the damage-inducible, error-prone DNA polymerase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and the catalytic component of the ImuA'-ImuB-DnaE2 mutagenesis cassette. It is a second, non-essential copy of the type-C polymerase alpha subunit: it is LexA-regulated and induced by all forms of DNA damage, is dispensable for chromosome replication, and lacks both the C-terminal clamp-loader-binding region and the PHP-domain exonuclease residues of the replicative DnaE1. Substituting its catalytic residues reproduces the deletion phenotype, so DnaE2 itself performs the synthesis past lesions. Through this activity it drives survival after UV irradiation, virulence in mice, and the emergence of drug resistance in vivo.

review.summary: A PAINT inference for polymerase activity placed in the DnaE/PolC family and seeded by the E. coli replicative alpha subunit.
review.reason: The IBD at PANTHER:PTN000793159 asserts DNA-directed DNA polymerase activity from UniProtKB:P10443, the E. coli DNA polymerase III alpha subunit. The node placement is the only question that matters here, and polymerase activity is the shared, defining chemistry of the whole PTHR32294 family: DnaE1, DnaE2 and PolC subfamilies alike. DnaE2 is a divergent paralog in process terms, but not in catalysis, and its catalytic residues are retained and functionally required.
